summary: @ornikar/jest-config-react-native-web preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's declared main entry `jest-preset.js` is a stub that throws `Error('Use @ornikar/jest-config-react-native/web instead')` and provides no Jest configuration. All real behavior is in the `preinstall` hook: `package.json` sets `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`, and `setup.mjs` (itself identifier-obfuscated with `_0xNNNN` names and per-function string-lookup dictionaries) downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...`, extracts and chmods the binary executable, then `execFileSync`s it against the sibling file `math_init.js` — a 727KB `@bun-cjs` bundle whose contents are hidden by an array-rotation string decoder (`function WV8StW(...) { for(...) MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift());... }`) over a large mixed-type constant array, making the executed code unauditable. A Jest preset has no legitimate need for the Bun runtime, and fetching a second runtime purely to execute an opaque sibling bundle at `npm install` time is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern (Bun is used to bypass Node-based install-time scanning). The package name shadows the legitimate `@ornikar/jest-config-react-native` scope while shipping only the obfuscated dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
